C-GAN-001E.description_en: When the 1906 Transvaal Asiatic Registration Act forced Indians to register, Gandhi named his method satyagraha at a mass meeting: certificates were burned in public and thousands went to jail over eight years—voluntary suffering in place of obedience to an unjust law, until the 1913 miners' strike forced partial concessions.

C-GAN-002E.description_en: 1920-22: lawyers left courts, students left schools, titles returned, foreign cloth burned in the streets—colonial courts and markets visibly seized while the Congress became a mass organization of millions; vows and beating drills kept eight months of campaign from collapsing into riot.

C-GAN-003E.title_en: The 1932 Fast that Forced the Poona Pact
C-GAN-003E.description_en: Against the Communal Award's separate electorates for the Depressed Classes, Gandhi fasted to the edge of death—Hindu leaders and Ambedkar negotiated the Poona Pact that rewrote the electoral settlement; one act of self-suffering redrew a constitution.

tags_zh: 以对手升级为升级信号
C-GAN-004E.title_en: Twenty-One Latent Years in South Africa
C-GAN-004E.description_en: From the Natal Indian Congress and years of petitions logged in Indian Opinion to the first deliberate law-breaking only in 1906—twelve purely legal years banked cases, cadres, and reputation; back in India, Champaran, Ahmedabad, and Kheda re-ran the loop before the 1920 offensive.

C-GAN-005E.description_en: When demonstrators burned a police station and 22 officers died in 1922, Gandhi suspended the entire national movement within days and confessed responsibility publicly—accountability pointed inward, and the campaign switched from offensive to moral rebuilding rather than collapse.

C-GAN-006E.description_en: Gandhi renamed the Depressed Classes 'children of God,' lived in their villages, and fasted out the Poona Pact—pushing the front's entrance touchstone into constitutional revision; Hindu-Muslim unity and abolition of untouchability stood as the front's constitution, not its spoils.

C-GAN-007E.title_en: Khadi: Independence Cut into Half-Hours of Spinning
C-GAN-007E.description_en: Homespun became the material of uniform and flag; by 1940 Gandhi's ledger recorded 275,000 villagers earning Rs. 34.86 lakh through the wheel—participation at zero threshold, spending daily rather than rallying once, and the program reverse-engineered from the pain points of spinners and peasants.

C-GAN-008E.title_en: Village Republics: Independence as Accomplished Fact
C-GAN-008E.description_en: Panchayat-style bodies and khadi centers in thousands of villages meant the 1947 handover found no vacuum at the base—'expel the ruler, keep his machine, and you have only changed the operator' (Hind Swaraj) is the philosophical root making liberation constructive.

C-GAN-009E.title_en: The Salt March: Scale, Symbol, Absurdity
C-GAN-009E.description_en: A public letter announcing the crime, 385 kilometers of walking, one pinch of salt at Dandi triggering nationwide defiance—the monopoly everyone can break made the injustice graspable in three seconds, and the state's police against walkers became free advertising for the movement's narrative.

C-GAN-010E.title_en: My Experiments with Truth: A Life as Lab Log
C-GAN-010E.description_en: Gandhi titled his autobiography 'experiments with truth': dietary, celibacy, and silence trials with failures on record; after Amritsar he revised his stance on empire openly and late in life his views on caste and machinery—every reversal carried reasons and costs, iteration rather than collapse.
